F1: isTeamAdmin(...) && isTeamOwner(...)` (lines 46-48) only passes OWNER, because `isTeamOwner` checks OWNER alone, so team ADMINs get FORBIDDEN.
F2: The env list is lowercased, but guests are matched raw with `includes(guest)`, so case changes and plus-addressing get past the blacklist.
F3: The return value of `updateCalendarAttendees` is ignored, and `updateAllCalendarEvents` catches its own errors, so the handler returns "Guests added" after the DB write even when the calendar update fails.
F4: The failure is still logged; leaving `err` out of the log hurts diagnosis but does not change behavior.
F5: The server schema has no uniqueness check, and the filter only compares against existing attendees, case-sensitively, so duplicate or case-variant guests in one request create duplicate attendee rows.
F6: The handler passes raw `guests` to `sendAddGuestsEmails`, so an existing attendee included in the request gets `AttendeeScheduledEmail` instead of the add-guests email.
F7: sendAddGuestsEmails` takes no event-type metadata and never checks the disable-host or disable-attendee email settings, unlike `sendLocationChangeEmails`.
F8: The handler checks only permissions, not booking status or end time, so a direct call can add guests to a cancelled or rejected booking and send invites.
F9: Attendees adding guests is an intended product choice; a missing size cap or rate limit is hardening, not a specific behavior defect.
F10: you_do_not_have_permission` is not in common.json or anywhere else, and the dialog renders `t(err.message)`, so users see the raw key.
F11: The new templates pass the raw key as `subject`, BaseScheduledEmail uses `props.subject || subject`, and BaseEmailHtml puts that in `<title>`, so the email title is the untranslated key.
F12: The new organizer email builds `from` with `APP_NAME` instead of `EMAIL_FROM_NAME`, so deployments that set a custom sender name get the wrong one.
F13: isInvalidEmail` is reset only by Cancel, so the error shows again on the next open after a success or a close via `onOpenChange`, and the template-literal message is never empty, so the fallback can't run.
F14: The new MultiEmail component hardcodes the English tooltip "Remove email" while it localizes its other strings with `t()`.
